# What is an SOP?
SOP stands for Standard Operating Procedures and is intended to provide a set of guidelines which outline the manner in which the station crew are expected to carry themselves over the course of a shift. Both departmental and overall SOP can be altered by the station’s Captain at any time with reasonable cause, although the captain may not ignore SOP outright.
It is best to consider this as a general code of conduct for your work, rather than an all-encompassing rulebook– You and your character's own intuition, judgement, and fallacies should shape the margins between what is black and white, and sometimes even bend the latter. SOP is not a checklist and should not be rigidly followed, especially in open and developing situations. It can be malleable as required by the situation, and the decision to enforce punishments for SOP breaches ultimately falls onto the Head of your department, Captain, and/or Central Command itself.
[bold]TL;DR:[/bold] The SOP tells you roughly what NT expects your job to look like. You don’t have to follow it, but if you ignore it consistently or in especially egregious ways you are a bad worker and will be treated as such.
# How does SOP help me? SOP gives you a code of conduct to abide by. You should follow what is in the following document, and repeated violations may result in contract termination, or removal from this sector.
SOP gives power to command to help determine what their department workers should be doing. It will help you guide the prospective hiring and firing of crew members.
Similarly, the SOP gives power to the crew, by allowing you to depose and fire relevant command members, as long as the reason is valid.
Central Command should be contacted for any questions regarding this SOP. This can be done via fax machine while on shift, or via provided hotlines otherwise
